review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–178). I grepped the library for the same patterns: `hQbox : Q ⊆ B ×ˢ J`, `fixed_pressure_cylinder_subset_ball` and `localBox_of_parabolic_ball hR`. The two main theorems share some setup. Both build `Q`, `B`, `J`, `η` and `hbox` (lines 67–71 and 145–149). Both prove `Q ⊆ B ×ˢ J` by rewriting `metricBall_eq_parabolicBall` (lines 74–78 and 151–155). Both derive `|η| ≤ 1` from `mollifiedBallCutoff_nonneg` and `mollifiedBallCutoff_le_one` (lines 104–106 and 170–172). Both obtain measurability of `w ↦ η w.1` from `mollifiedBallCutoff_smooth ... .continuous.measurable.comp measurable_fst` (lines 98–99 and 165–166). Each repeated piece is only a few lines of routine unfolding or API composition. A shared helper such as a `Q ⊆ B ×ˢ J` lemma would be a thin wrapper and would not remove nontrivial reasoning. The rest of the proofs differ: the first uses Morrey-norm monotonicity and the tensor estimate, the second uses `MemLp` exponent monotonicity on a finite measure. Other uses of `localBox_of_parabolic_ball` in the library are single-line calls and do not repeat a proof block. Under this rubric I found no justified finding. The only uncertainty is whether a reviewer would count the roughly 8-line setup duplication as enough, and I judged it not to be.
